title: K-map grouping for F = B'D' + BD

steps.caption: A 4x4 K-map. Rows are AB and columns are CD, in Gray-code order (00, 01, 11, 10), so neighbouring cells differ in exactly one variable. 1s mark where F is true.
Group 1s in rectangles of size 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16. Start with the four 1s in the middle. Rows 01 and 11 and columns 01 and 11 share B = 1 and D = 1.
Inside the group A and C change but B and D do not. Variables that change drop out. This group is simply BD.
The map wraps around like a torus: the left edge touches the right edge, and the top touches the bottom. So the four corners form one group of four.
In the corner group B = 0 and D = 0 never change, while A and C do. That group is B'D'. All 1s are covered, so add the two products.
